item.title: AI Rally Loses Steam, US-China Talks Persist
item.description: US equity futures waver after Meta, Alibaba and Tencent boosted investor optimism around AI with their latest technology. The US and China held a second round of trade talks ahead of the Trump-Xi summit. President Trump is set to speak as the UN General Assembly convenes in New York City. Kallum Pickering of Peel Hunt joins "Bloomberg Brief" to discuss the sustainability of debt-financed growth. This video has been edited to correct a graphic to show that the latest AI trade faltered in the Asian session. The correction is placed at 01:01 (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Record Oil Supertanker Rates Make Waves for the Whole Fleet
item.description: High earnings for the biggest oil carriers are spreading to smaller vessels.
item.dc:creator: Alex Longley

item.title: Dangote Hires Engineers India for $16 Billion Kenya Refinery
item.description: Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest person, has hired the engineers that built his Lagos refinery to work on the new crude processing plant in Kenya that he is set to start constructing this month.
item.dc:creator: Emele Onu

item.title: US Borrowing Way Too Much Money: Pickering
item.description: Kallum Pickering, Peel Hunt Chief Economist, joins Bloomberg's Vonnie Quinn on "Bloomberg Brief" to discuss the risks around rising debt-fueled growth. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Europe’s Power Exchange Giant EEX Eyes New Weather Futures
item.description: European Energy Exchange AG, the world’s biggest power bourse, is considering listing new weather futures, becoming the latest commodity platform to expand into products tied to renewable energy’s growing role in electricity generation.
item.dc:creator: Mary Hui and Joe Wertz

item.title: Ecuador Seeks US Help Fighting $30-Billion Cocaine Trade
item.description: Ecuador is asking the US "every day" for more help fighting a cocaine trade President Daniel Noboa estimates is worth $30 billion a year. In an interview with Bloomberg Television's Francine Lacqua in New York on Sept. 21, Noboa said Ecuador is "going after the big fish" and needs help from the US and Europe. He says about 1,200 tons of cocaine move through Ecuador each year, with roughly 80% destined for the US and Europe. But Noboa says Ecuador will remain in charge of all operations, saying the country would "never give a blank check to any country." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cristina Caffarra: EU Agencies ‘Infantilize’ European Countries
item.description: European countries need to move away from their reliance on EU governing bodies to make decisions and take matters into their own hands says Cristina Caffarra, Founder and Chair of the Eurostack Initiative. She spoke to Bloomberg's Guy Johnson on 'The Pulse'. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Urges EU to Keep Auto Markets Open, Avoid Protectionism
item.description: China’s Commerce Minister Wang Wentao called on the European Union to keep its markets open to Chinese automakers and avoid protectionism to ensure a “fair, open and non-discriminatory” environment.
item.dc:creator: Foster Wong

item.title: Tech Rally Loses Steam In Europe as Oil Rises
item.description:
A rally in technology stocks came to a halt as oil resumed its role in setting the tone for markets, with Brent heading for its first gain in a week as investors tracked diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war. Earlier, stocks got a lift after Meta’s new artificial intelligence agent, Muse, quickly rose to the top of mobile app charts.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards and Guy Johnson.
Correct: Graphic edited at 01;00;19;11, 01;27;09;02, 01;34;40;22 to clarify that Ermotti said fee pools in banking are going be down, with UBS in-line with market trends. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Demand Surges at South African Bond Auction Ahead of Rate Call
item.description: Demand surged at an auction of South African government bonds as investors snapped up relatively high yields ahead of inflation data and a central bank policy meeting later this week.
item.dc:creator: Mpho Hlakudi

item.title: Oil Analyst Sankey Sees ‘Very Elevated’ Market Through End of 2027
item.description: Paul Sankey, president at Sankey Research, warns of oil market risk from tightness in US refining capacity as diesel reaches new record highs. Sankey discusses the effects of a potential US diesel export ban and the lingering impacts he sees for the global oil market through the end of this year and into 2027. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dimon Says US Shouldn’t Punish India Over Russian Oil: CNBC TV18
item.description: India and global oil markets shouldn’t be punished as the US seeks to pressure Russia to end its war in Ukraine, JPMorgan Chase & Co. Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon said in an interview, pointing to the challenges refiners face in switching crude supplies.
item.dc:creator: Anup Roy

item.title: Yields Can Fall on Good Oil News, Bad Eco Data, JPM’s Berro Says
item.description: Kelsey Berro, fixed income portfolio manager at JPMorgan Asset Management, explains the geopolitical and economic catalysts she sees stabilizing US Treasury yields. She speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia’s Valuation Comes Back Down to Earth
item.description: The shares sell for half the multiple they fetched in 2025.
item.dc:creator: Phil Serafino

item.title: Indonesia to Form New Body to Oversee Land Conflicts, Reform
item.description: Indonesia will form a new body to oversee land reform and settle related conflicts in a bid to address longstanding problems that have plagued plantations, mines, farmers and indigenous communities.
item.dc:creator: Norman Harsono

item.title: Alibaba Unveils Powerful AI Chip as Meta Revives AI Optimism
item.description:
"The Pulse With Francine Lacqua" is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.
Today's guests: Mike Bell, RBC BlueBay Head of Market Strategy; Kristina Spohr, London School of Economics Professor; Cristina Caffarra, EuroStack Initiative Founder & Chair (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Luxury Earnings Estimates Look Too Optimistic, RBC Analysts Say
item.description: Market expectations for earnings at European luxury-goods makers are overly optimistic given softening demand conditions and buying trends, according to analysts at RBC.
item.dc:creator: Levin Stamm

item.title: Tycoon Buys Mumbai Tower for $74 Million in Record Home Deal
item.description: The founder of one of India’s biggest retail stockbrokers snapped up a luxury tower in Mumbai for 7.11 billion rupees ($74.3 million), marking the most expensive known purchase of a single residential unit in the country.
item.dc:creator: Ranjani Raghavan

item.title: US Stocks Hold Gains Ahead of Trump’s UN Address: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks held steady after a rally in the artificial-intelligence trade as falling oil prices kept setting the tone for markets, with investors tracking diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Andre Janse van Vuuren and Julien Ponthus

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 22
item.description: Oil turned lower as Saudi Arabia sought to resume flows on a vital pipeline and traders weighed signs of diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Charles Gorrivan and Alex Longley
